messages.author: e1b754c34a3fc1a2
messages.subject: WLSMV estimator + theta parameterization, residual constraint
parts:
Dear all,

For my measurement invariance test, I want to constraint loadings, thresholds and residuals between two groups ("Time" 1&2). I want to compare the Strong model (loadings, thresholds) and Strict model (loadings, thresholds and residuals). My CFA model is WLSMV estimated with Theta parameterization.  When I do this I get this error massage: 
> semTools:::difftest(Strong, Strict)
Error in solve.default(P1) : 
  system is computationally singular: reciprocal condition number = 1.31615e-18

> anova(Strong, Strict)
Error in solve.default(P1) : 
  system is computationally singular: reciprocal condition number = 1.31615e-18

> lavTestLRT(Strong, Strict)
Error in solve.default(P1) : 
  system is computationally singular: reciprocal condition number = 1.31615e-18

> fitMeasures(Strong, "cfi") - fitMeasures(Strict, "cfi")
  cfi 
0.021 

> fitMeasures(Strong, "chisquare") - fitMeasures(Strict, "chisquare")
numeric(0)

My syntax is:

Datsub12 <- subset(Data12, Time == "1" | Time == "2")

model <- 'PDS=~ AGGR + AGOR + ANXI + COGN + MOOD + SOMA + SOPH
AGOR =~ SQ4 + SQ8 + SQ14 + SQ25
ANXI =~ SQ48 + SQ24 + SQ28 + SQ33 + SQ41 + SQ46
COGN =~ SQ2 + SQ6 + SQ39 + SQ44 + SQ47
MOOD =~ SQ13 + SQ7 + SQ3 + SQ19 + SQ38 + SQ40
SOMA =~ SQ31 + SQ5 + Q11 + SQ17 + SQ22 + SQ26 + SQ1
SOPH =~ SQ32 + SQ27 + SQ23 + SQ36 + SQ45
AGGR =~ SQ43 + SQ10 + SQ16 + SQ21'

Strong <- cfa(model, group="Time", data=Data12, estimator="WLSMV", parameterization="theta", ordered=names(Data12)[2:38], std.lv=T , group.equal= c("loadings", "thresholds"))

Strict <- cfa(model, group="Time", data=Data12, estimator="WLSMV", parameterization="theta", ordered=names(Data12)[2:38], std.lv=T , group.equal= c("loadings", "thresholds", "residuals"))

Does anyone know what this error message means and what I can do about it?

Thank you!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: WLSMV estimator + theta parameterization, residual constraint
parts:
> lavTestLRT(Strong, Strict)
Error in solve.default(P1) : 
  system is computationally singular: reciprocal condition number = 1.31615e-18

Did both of your models converge?  Was lavaan able to calculate SEs for both models?  

inspect(Strong, "converged")
inspect(Strong, "se")
inspect(Strict, "converged")
inspect(Strict, "se")

> fitMeasures(Strong, "chisquare") - fitMeasures(Strict, "chisquare")
numeric(0)

There is no "chisquare" returned by fitMeasures().  Instead, it is called "chisq".  The "numeric(0)" means it is an empty numeric vector, and it's empty because there is nothing called "chisquare" to report.


Terry

messages.subject: Re: WLSMV estimator + theta parameterization, residual constraint
parts: Both models seem to be converged (> inspect(Strong, "converged") [1] TRUE) although lavaan was not able to calculate SEs (only zero's).  What does this mean?

I think it means the covariance matrix of parameter (point) estimates (or the gradient or something that is used to find that matrix) cannot be inverted.  I'm not crystal clear about the details of the WLS estimation algorithm, but here is an article that provides some details about estimating SEs in WLSMV, as well as their robust corrections.

http://dx.doi.org/10.1080/10705511.2013.824793

Terry

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: WLSMV estimator + theta parameterization, residual constraint
parts: Is there a way to constrain residual errors between two groups by hand? Something like:   'SQ21~~ c(T1, T2)*SQ21' ?

Yes, you can constrain residual variances across groups that way.  But to be clear those are parameter estimates, not to be confused with the standard errors (SE) of those estimates (i.e., how much we expect a parameter estimate to vary across many samples from the same population, using the same methods, etc.).  You cannot fix a SE (nor would you want to) without simply fixing the parameter itself to a value that you are then treating as known with 100% certainty.
No I didn't get a warning, I actually get all zeroes.

Standard errors were all zeros, or parameter estimates of residual variances were all zeros?

Terry

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: WLSMV estimator + theta parameterization, residual constraint
parts: The chi-square of constraints "loading, threshold" is the same as constraint "loading, threshold and residual".

This sounds like you are using the "group.equal" argument, but you are already making the constraints in the model syntax -- specifications in the syntax character string will override any options used in the call to lavaan() or cfa().  To fit a model without those constraints, you need to save a different model syntax without those labels (or at least don't use identical labels for both groups).

Again, it would be easier for people to help you if you provided your entire R script, including your call(s) to the cfa() function.

Terry

In this model, you need to manually free up the residual variances of
the second group. So you need add the following lines:

SQ43~~ c(1, NA)*SQ43
SQ10~~ c(1, NA)*SQ10
SQ16~~ c(1, NA)*SQ16
SQ21~~ c(1, NA)*SQ21

In the StrictAGGR model, they will be fixed to 1.0 in both groups.

Yves.
